content.title: About
content.content: Pad Thai with chicken is a popular Thai dish made from rice noodles stir‑fried with chicken breast, egg, tofu, bean sprouts, peanuts, and aromatic spices. The sauce typically combines tamarind, fish sauce, sugar and lime, giving the dish a sweet‑sour flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the 1930s in Bangkok as a quick street‑food snack.
It is traditionally served with a lime wedge, fresh cilantro and extra crushed peanuts.
Tamarind, the key ingredient of the sauce, comes from the Tamarindus indica tree, native to Africa but widely cultivated in Southeast Asia.
Original recipes use rice noodles about 5 mm wide, though variations use thicker or thinner noodles.
Pad Thai is often considered Thailand’s “national dish,” despite many regional variations.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken breast and tofu provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice noodles supply slowly digestible carbohydrates that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The tamarind‑fish sauce blend contains vitamin B6, which supports protein metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts and a modest amount of vegetable oil deliver monounsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lime and cilantro are rich in vitamin C and polyphenols that combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts used in the dish can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Fish sauce and soy sauce can add a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten in soy sauce
items.content: Traditional soy sauce may contain gluten; gluten‑free alternatives should be used for celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The oil and peanuts make the dish relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Pad Thai hot, garnished with a lime wedge, fresh cilantro and a sprinkle of crushed peanuts. Add chili sauce to taste if you like heat. It is typically eaten with a fork or chopsticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Pad Thai is best enjoyed fresh. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. When reheating, add a splash of water to keep the noodles from drying out.
